{{other uses|König's theorem (disambiguation)}}
In [[kinetics (physics)|kinematics]], '''König's theorem''' or '''König's decomposition''' is a mathematical relation derived by [[Johann Samuel König]] that assists with the calculations of angular momentum and kinetic energy of bodies and systems of particles.

== For a system of particles ==
The theorem is divided in two parts. 

=== First part of König's theorem ===

The first part expresses the [[angular momentum]] of a system as the sum of the [[angular momentum]] of the [[centre of mass]] and the [[angular momentum]] applied to the particles relative to the [[center of mass]]. <ref>{{cite journal |last1=Essén |first1=Hanno |title=Average Angular Velocity |journal=European Journal of Physics |year=1993 |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=201–205 |doi=10.1088/0143-0807/14/5/002 |arxiv=physics/0401146 |bibcode=1993EJPh...14..201E |s2cid=250879804 }}</ref>

<math>\displaystyle \vec{L} = \vec{r}_{CoM} \times \sum\limits_{i} m_{i} \vec{v}_{CoM} + \vec{L}'= \vec{L}_{CoM} + \vec{L}'</math>

==== Proof ====

Considering an [[inertial reference frame]] with origin O, the [[angular momentum]] of the system can be defined as:

<math>\vec{L} = \sum\limits_{i} (\vec{r}_{i} \times m_{i} \vec{v}_{i} )</math>

The position of a single particle can be expressed as:

<math>\vec{r}_{i} = \vec{r}_{CoM} + \vec{r}'_{i}</math>

And so we can define the velocity of a single particle: 

<math>\vec{v}_{i} = \vec{v}_{CoM} + \vec{v}'_{i}</math>

The first equation becomes: 

:<math>\vec{L} = \sum\limits_{i} (\vec{r}_{CoM} + \vec{r}'_{i}) \times m_{i} (\vec{v}_{CoM} + \vec{v}'_{i})</math>

:<math>\vec{L} = \sum\limits_{i} \vec{r}'_{i} \times m_{i} \vec{v}'_{i} + \left( \sum\limits_{i} m_{i}\vec{r}'_{i}\right) \times  \vec{v}_{CoM} + \vec{r}_{CoM} \times \sum\limits_{i} m_{i} \vec{v}'_{i} + \sum\limits_{i} \vec{r}_{CoM} \times m_{i} \vec{v}_{CoM}</math>

But the following terms are equal to zero:

<math>\sum\limits_{i} m_{i} \vec{r}'_{i} = 0</math>

<math>\sum\limits_{i} m_{i} \vec{v}'_{i} = 0</math>

So we prove that:

<math>\vec{L} =   \sum\limits_{i} \vec{r}'_{i} \times m_{i} \vec{v}'_{i}+M \vec{r}_{CoM} \times  \vec{v}_{CoM}</math>

where  M is the total [[mass]] of the system.

=== Second part of König's theorem === 

The second part expresses the [[kinetic energy]] of a system of particles in terms of the velocities of the individual particles and the [[centre of mass]].

Specifically, it states that the [[kinetic energy]] of a system of particles is the sum of the [[kinetic energy]] associated to the movement of the [[center of mass]] and the [[kinetic energy]] associated to the movement of the particles relative to the [[center of mass]].<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Essén |first1=Hanno |title=Average Angular Velocity |journal=European Journal of Physics |year=1993 |volume=14 |issue=5 |pages=201–205 |doi=10.1088/0143-0807/14/5/002 |arxiv=physics/0401146 |bibcode=1993EJPh...14..201E |s2cid=250879804 }}</ref>

<math>K = K' + K_{\text{CoM}}</math>

==== Proof ====

The total [[kinetic energy]] of the system is:

<math>K = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i v_i^2</math>

Like we did in the first part, we substitute the velocity:

:<math>K = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i |\bar v'_i + \bar v_\text{CoM}|^2</math> 

:<math>K = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i (\bar v'_i + \bar v_\text{CoM})\cdot(\bar v'_i + \bar v_\text{CoM}) = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i {v'_i}^2 + \bar v_\text{CoM} \cdot \sum_i m_i \bar v'_i + \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i v_\text{CoM}^2</math>

We know that <math>\bar v_{CoM}\cdot\sum_im_i \bar v'_i = 0,</math> so if we define:

<math>K' = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i {v'_i}^2</math>

<math>K_\text{CoM} = \sum_i \frac{1}{2} m_i v_\text{CoM}^2 = \frac 12 M v_\text{CoM}^2</math>

we're left with:

<math>K = K' + K_\text{CoM}</math>

== For a rigid body ==
The theorem can also be applied to [[rigid bodies]], stating that the kinetic energy K of a rigid body, as viewed by an observer fixed in some inertial [[Frame of reference|reference frame]] N, can be written as:

<math>^{N}K = \frac{1}{2} m \cdot {^N\mathbf{\bar{v}}} \cdot {^N\mathbf{\bar{v}}} + \frac{1}{2} {^N\!\mathbf{\bar{H}}} \cdot ^{N}{\!\!\mathbf{\omega}}^R </math>

where <math>{m}</math> is the mass of the rigid body; <math>{^N\mathbf{\bar{v}}}</math> is the velocity of the center of mass of the rigid body, as viewed by an observer fixed in an inertial frame N; <math>{^N\!\mathbf{\bar{H}}}</math> is the [[angular momentum]] of the rigid body about the center of mass, also taken in the inertial frame N; and <math>^{N}{\!\!\mathbf{\omega}}^R</math> is the angular velocity of the rigid body R relative to the inertial frame N.<ref>{{cite book |last=Rao |first=Anil V. |title=Dynamics of Particles and Rigid Bodies: A Systematic Approach |publisher=Cambridge University Press |page=421}}</ref>
